problem_identification.critical_issue: Cross-stream tensor handoff without record_stream in graph-captured pipeline causes allocator-reuse data race
evidence: Outputs are not close (atol=0.01, rtol=0.01). max_abs_err=8.493e+00, mean_abs_err=6.082e-01
this kernel's output depends on what the CUDA caching allocator previously stored, on shape 8x256x64x128
problem_identification.root_cause: The stage-offset pipeline allocates xl[k]/z[k] on sMem and consumes them on sConv (and y1/y2 vice-versa), then frees them (`= None`) immediately. The graph-capture call path uses rec=False, so no record_stream/event protects the blocks; the caching allocator hands the same memory to the next sMem allocation while sConv still reads it, so conv/GN inputs contain stale or unwritten data. The known-good kernel keeps each chunk's whole chain on one stream, avoiding this entirely.
problem_identification.trigger_condition: B>=2 so the two-stream pipeline is taken, and the captured graph (rec=False) frees a tensor on one stream while the other stream still reads it.
must_hold_invariants: every intermediate is produced and consumed on the same stream, or its lifetime is protected by an event/record_stream
no tensor is freed while another stream's pending kernel still reads it
gn stats psum/psq slots read by gn_final are all written by gn_stats
problem_identification.minimal_fix: Keep each chunk's full chain (transpose, conv1, GN, conv2, epilogue) on one stream, as in the known-good _run_pipeline; do not split conv onto sConv and GN onto sMem.
